what: Convert R objects to JSON and back
title: glazelite: fast JSON reading and writing for R
text: Dates date-times written strings, unbox() marks single values become arrays: Arrays records come back data frames, arrays scalars vectors, arrays arrays matrices:
code: library(glazelite)  toJSON(list(id = 1L, tags = c("a", "b"), ok = TRUE), auto_unbox = TRUE) #> {"id":1,"tags":["a","b"],"ok":true}  df <- data.frame(id = 1:2, name = c("Ada", "Grace"), score = c(9.5, NA)) toJSON(df) #> [{"id":1,"name":"Ada","score":9.5},{"id":2,"name":"Grace"}]  toJSON(df, dataframe = "columns", pretty = TRUE) #> { #>   "id": [1, 2], #>   "name": ["Ada", "Grace"], #>   "score": [9.5, null] #> }  toJSON(array(1:8, c(2, 2, 2))) #> [[[1,5],[3,7]],[[2,6],[4,8]]] toJSON(data.frame(day = as.Date("2026-01-31"), n = 3L)) #> [{"day":"2026-01-31","n":3}]  toJSON(list(id = unbox(7L), tags = "a")) #> {"id":7,"tags":["a"]}  toJSON(pi, digits = 3) #> [3.142] fromJSON('[{"id":1,"name":"Ada","score":9.5},{"id":2,"name":"Grace"}]') #>   id  name score #> 1  1   Ada   9.5 #> 2  2 Grace    NA  fromJSON("[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]") #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    1    2    3 #> [2,]    4    5    6  str(fromJSON('{"id": 1, "tags": ["a", "b"], "nested": {"ok": true, "x": [1.5, null]}}')) #> List of 3 #>  $ id    : int 1 #>  $ tags  : chr [1:2] "a" "b" #>  $ nested:List of 2 #>   ..$ ok: logi TRUE #>   ..$ x : num [1:2] 1.5 NA

title: glazelite: fast JSON reading and writing for R
text: glazelite uses jsonlite’s function names argument names, common code keeps working library(jsonlite) replaced library(glazelite). covers toJSON(), fromJSON(), write_json(), read_json(), stream_in(), stream_out(), unbox(), prettify(), minify() validate(). JSON structure jsonlite’s vectors, arrays every shape, lists, dates date-times, data frame layouts including row names. digits set, numbers rounded written exactly jsonlite writes . package’s tests check jsonlite. Two defaults differ purpose: Numbers keep full precision: every double written shortest text reads back value. jsonlite rounds four decimal digits default, toJSON(pi) [3.1416] [3.141592653589793] . Use digits = 4 jsonlite’s output. Missing non-finite numbers written null. jsonlite writes strings "NA", "NaN" "Inf"; na = "string" . yyjsonr, fastest JSON package R, makes different trade-: interface (write_json_str(), read_json_str(), options objects), writes differs jsonlite places. default options (jsonlite digits = NA, yyjsonr 0.1.22): glazelite cover jsonlite. missing different: Complex raw vectors, objects classes factors, dates date-times, raise error instead converted. default digits = NA, exponents written 1E20 rather 1e+20. valid JSON number. Duplicated names list written ; jsonlite makes unique. reading, arrays mixed types stay lists instead coerced character, arrays records whose fields hold arrays objects stay lists records, jsonlite returns data frame list columns. flatten argument available. fromJSON() reads JSON string file path, URL. serializeJSON(), rbind_pages() base64 helpers provided.

title: Convert an R object to JSON text — toJSON
text: x atomic vector, array, list, data frame. Array dimensions written existing order, including dimensions length one zero. Data frames may contain matrix, list, data-frame columns. dataframe Data frame layout: rows, columns, values. Date Encode Date objects ISO 8601 strings "2026-01-31" ("ISO8601", default) number days since 1970-01-01 ("epoch"). POSIXt Encode date-times strings format R prints ("string", default), ISO 8601 strings ("ISO8601"), milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC ("epoch"), MongoDB-style objects {"$date": 1767323045000} ("mongo"). factor Encode factors level labels ("string", default) integer level indices ("integer"). null Encode NULL empty object, {} ("list", default), JSON null ("null"). na Encode missing non-finite values JSON null strings. auto_unbox Whether length-one atomic vectors become scalars. Use jsonlite::unbox() mark individual values instead. digits NA (default) writes every number shortest text reads back value. number gives maximum number decimal digits, number wrapped () number significant digits; round jsonlite . pretty Whether indent output: TRUE two spaces per level, number spaces. Pretty file output ends newline. always_decimal Distinguish doubles integers retaining decimal point exponent finite double output. UTC Whether date-times converted UTC. POSIXt = "ISO8601" strings end Z. rownames Whether row names data frames written, _row field. default, NULL, writes character row names automatic ones.
